items.title: Michael Abene interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 11, 2003
items.q: The transcript identifies Monk Rowe as the interviewer ('[INTERVIEWER] My name is Monk Rowe...') and Michael Abene as the interviewee. No personal or professional relationship beyond the interview context is described.

ctx.x: Michael was interviewed in Toronto, Canada on January 11, 2003 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.

My name is Monk Rowe and we are in Toronto at the IAJE convention. And I’m very pleased to have Michael Abene with me today. We were just talking about the challenge of trying to show people what you do in 50 minutes.

Yes. It’s very interesting because I’m so used to doing two and three hour seminars. And the thing is when you do 50 minutes it’s so — you know you talk about being confined, especially in the subject, in this instance of talking about writing for big band and symphony combined, which is a course that the late Manny Albam and I initiated at Manhattan School of Music and along with the help of Justin DeCioccio, who is the head of the jazz department there. So you’re talking about quite a — it’s not, you’re not…
